correctness.rationale: For epsilon-free transition-bipartite unary NFA, any repeated-state subrun has even length; deleting it preserves acceptance and the parity of a run. The first word in each accepted parity therefore has a simple run. Shortest accepted length tn gives at least tn+1 states, and when n is odd the first opposite-parity accepted length (t+1)n requires at least (t+1)n+1 states. The explicit even-n path with return cycle n and odd-n path with return cycle 2n recognize exactly the requested length progressions in transition-bipartite cactus graphs, with all n>=2,t>=1 boundary cases including n=2. Independently reconstructed witness transitions at n=3,4 and verified the general path/cycle argument from actual RESULT.md and checker.py; finite checker ranges cannot be proofs.
